stem: A visitor from another country asks to buy one small package containing 60 mg total pseudoephedrine. The visitor has only a foreign passport and no identification document accepted by the federal CMEA retail-ID rule. The sale otherwise stays within all quantity limits. Which federal point is most relevant?

choices.text: A foreign passport always satisfies the CMEA retail-ID requirement for any pseudoephedrine quantity.
The sale is prohibited because every pseudoephedrine purchase, including a 60 mg single package, requires the ordinary logbook and ID process.
A single sales package containing no more than 60 mg may use the narrow exception from the ordinary purchaser-ID and logbook transaction requirement.
The pharmacist may waive identification for any purchase under the 3.6 gram daily limit.
The visitor may buy any amount if another adult with acceptable identification signs the logbook instead.

explanation.core_reasoning: This is not a gram-limit question. The decisive fact is that the request is for one sales package containing no more than 60 mg, which DEA identifies as a narrow exception to the ordinary individual ID/logbook transaction requirement.

choice_analysis.A: DEA guidance states that a foreign passport does not itself satisfy the ordinary CMEA identification rule described for these purchases.
choice_analysis.B: Federal law provides a narrow single-package exception at no more than 60 mg.
choice_analysis.C: DEA identifies this narrow exception for one sales package containing no more than 60 mg of pseudoephedrine.
choice_analysis.D: The daily quantity limit and the separate ID/logbook gate are different requirements.
choice_analysis.E: The purchaser's own identity and transaction must satisfy the applicable rule; another person cannot simply sign in place of the purchaser.

related_facts: CMEA quantity limits and ID/logbook rules are separate gates.
The 60 mg rule is a narrow single-package exception, not a general low-dose waiver.
explanation.mpje_trap: Passing the daily quantity limit does not answer the ID question; look for the single-package 60 mg exception.

reasoning_steps: Separate quantity compliance from purchaser-ID compliance
